summary: The session component is the loop's state and persistence substrate: the 'learn' stage's memory and the control stage's resume anchor. ToolCache and LlmCache (cache.rs) avoid redundant act and reason work by keying results on tool+args and on embedding/context_hash similarity; EditHistory (edit_history.rs) records every mutation as a branchable EditCheckpoint of FileSnapshots for undo/redo/timeline; CheckpointManager (checkpoint.rs) snapshots the whole TaskCheckpoint — step, iteration, messages, tool logs, errors, budget — via CheckpointDelta writes for crash-safe resume; EncryptionManager (encryption.rs) protects data at rest with AES-256-GCM and zeroizes its key on drop; LocalFirstCoordinator (local_first.rs) caches responses for offline use; ChatStore (chat_store.rs) persists encrypted named conversations.
context_basis: Recommendations formed with src/session/ read in the context of the full engine (~600k budget framing), grounded in cache.rs ToolCache/LlmCache/CacheManager, edit_history.rs EditCheckpoint/EditHistory/TimelineEntry, checkpoint.rs TaskCheckpoint/CheckpointDelta/CheckpointManager, encryption.rs EncryptionManager, local_first.rs LocalFirstCoordinator, and chat_store.rs ChatStore.

examples.title: Cache a read-only tool result
examples.intent: Skip re-executing a read-only tool whose inputs have not changed.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolCache::get keys on cache_key(tool_name, args_json) and returns a hit inside its TTL, so the act stage short-circuits and the loop spends its budget on new work instead of repeat reads.

outputs_to: cached ToolResult into the act stage

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a read node opens its cache card; a hit lights a shortcut edge straight to the stored value.
touch_interaction.visual: Cache-hit nodes show a lightning badge and skip their execution spinner; misses show a hollow badge.

examples.mini_scenario: The agent repeats grep_search with identical args; ToolCache::get returns the stored result in microseconds and the act stage moves on without touching the filesystem.
examples.pitfall: Only cache tools that pass is_cacheable — caching a mutating tool's result serves stale state to the loop.

examples.title: Invalidate cache entries by path
examples.intent: Drop only the cache entries a mutation could have affected.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: After a mutating act, CacheManager::invalidate_path removes every ToolCache entry whose key contains the touched path, so post-write reads re-run against fresh state while unrelated cached results survive.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a write node's output edge across the cache node clears only the cards matching that path.
touch_interaction.visual: Path-matching cache cards fade out; unrelated cards stay lit, and the hit-rate dial barely dips.

examples.mini_scenario: file_edit lands on config.rs; invalidate_path drops the two config.rs entries so the next file_read re-scans, while the cached Cargo.toml read stays hot.
examples.pitfall: Over-broad invalidation (clear() on every write) forfeits the entire cache saving on unrelated reads.

examples.title: Evict expired and LRU entries on overflow
examples.intent: Keep the cache inside a fixed memory budget without stalling the loop.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ToolCache::set calls evict_expired at max_entries (1000 by default) and then removes the oldest 10% LRU slice, so the cache stays bounded and set never blocks the act stage.

outputs_to: CacheStats entry_count settling under the cap

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the cache node compacts it, visibly dropping greyed expired cards and the oldest entries.
touch_interaction.visual: An entry-count gauge sits under the max line; expired cards grey and fall away during the pinch.

examples.mini_scenario: The cache hits 1000 entries mid-task; the next set evicts 100 oldest and the loop continues without a hiccup.
examples.pitfall: Setting max_entries too low thrashes the cache — entries are evicted before their TTL and hit_rate collapses.

examples.title: Match a semantic LLM cache hit
examples.intent: Reuse a prior LLM response for a near-identical prompt instead of paying for a new call.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: LlmCache::lookup matches on cosine similarity of the prompt embedding plus a context_hash and model check, so a repeated reason turn can be served from cache and skip a billable, latency-heavy model call.

inputs_from: agent (reason-turn prompt embedding, context_hash, model id)
outputs_to: cached LLM response into the reason stage

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the reason node fans out nearby cached prompts as orbit cards ordered by similarity distance.
touch_interaction.visual: A matching card snaps onto the node with a similarity-score badge; near misses hover dimmer at their distance.

examples.mini_scenario: The agent re-asks the same diagnostic question with an unchanged context_hash; lookup returns the cached answer and the loop skips a full model round-trip.
examples.pitfall: Ignoring context_hash serves an answer computed under different context and silently misleads the reason stage.

examples.title: Snapshot a file before it changes
examples.intent: Capture the exact prior file state so any edit can be undone.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EditHistory::create_checkpoint records FileSnapshots (path, content, size, hash) tagged with an EditAction before the mutation lands, giving the loop a durable rollback point per act.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a write node drops a snapshot pin capturing the file's pre-edit state before the act fires.
touch_interaction.visual: A camera-pin badge appears on the timeline edge with the file hash; the write node pauses until the pin sets.

examples.mini_scenario: Before file_edit applies a patch, create_checkpoint snapshots the original content so a later /undo restores it byte-for-byte.
examples.pitfall: Snapshotting after the edit instead of before loses the original content and makes undo restore the wrong state.

examples.title: Undo the last edit checkpoint
examples.intent: Roll the workspace back to the state before a bad edit so the loop can retry.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EditHistory::undo steps the position pointer back (can_undo gate) and restores the checkpoint's FileSnapshots, letting the loop recover from a wrong turn without restarting the task or its budget.

outputs_to: agent retry with a different fix

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Dragging the current-checkpoint marker left along the timeline scrubs back one step and restores that snapshot.
touch_interaction.visual: The marker slides to the previous pin; the restored file card flashes green and the undone pin dims.

examples.mini_scenario: An edit breaks the build; /undo restores the pre-edit snapshot and the agent's next reason turn proposes a different fix.
examples.pitfall: Undoing past a git-anchored checkpoint without accounting for it desyncs the working tree from committed history.

examples.title: Branch the edit timeline after an undo
examples.intent: Preserve alternate edit paths instead of silently discarding them.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: After an undo, a new create_checkpoint truncates the redo future on the current branch, while create_branch / switch_to_main model the timeline as a tree of what-if edit paths the loop explored.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing a branch edge from an earlier checkpoint pin spawns a labeled alternate edit path.
touch_interaction.visual: The timeline forks into a colored branch line with its own pins; the abandoned redo path greys but stays visible.

examples.mini_scenario: The user undoes two edits, then the agent tries a different approach; the timeline forks so the abandoned path remains inspectable.
examples.pitfall: Assuming a linear timeline after undo silently discards the redo branch the loop may have meant to keep.

examples.title: Render the edit timeline for restore-point picking
examples.intent: Project the loop's mutation history so the user can pick a restore point.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EditHistory::timeline emits TimelineEntry rows (id, is_current, action, timestamp, branch) — read-only data that feeds /timeline without touching loop control.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Two-finger-rotate on the timeline pivots the view between the main line and branch lines.
touch_interaction.visual: Each entry is a labeled pin with its action icon; the current pin glows and each branch gets a distinct hue.

examples.mini_scenario: The user opens /timeline, rotates to inspect a side branch, and taps a pin to goto that checkpoint.
examples.pitfall: Rendering entries without branch labels makes divergent edit paths indistinguishable and invites restoring the wrong line.

examples.title: Save the loop's TaskCheckpoint
examples.intent: Persist enough state to resume the loop after an interruption.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CheckpointManager::save writes a TaskCheckpoint holding current_step, current_iteration, messages, tool_calls, errors, and estimated cumulative tokens, so continue_execution can rehydrate the loop exactly where it stopped.

outputs_to: resume path in the control stage

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the control hub drops a task-checkpoint pin capturing the entire loop state.
touch_interaction.visual: The save pin shows step/iteration and a token-total badge, pulsing once on write completion.

examples.mini_scenario: Mid-task the manager saves; after a crash, load restores step, iteration, and messages and the loop continues.
examples.pitfall: Persisting messages but not the cumulative token count lets a resumed loop blow past its original budget ceiling.

examples.title: Write incremental checkpoint deltas
examples.intent: Persist progress cheaply every turn without rewriting the whole checkpoint.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: save prefers compute_delta CheckpointDelta writes (new messages, tool calls, errors since a base version) and compacts into a fresh base after the delta chain grows, keeping per-turn persistence lightweight.

inputs_from: per-turn state diffs vs base version (compute_delta)

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the checkpoint node expands a layer stack of thin delta cards over the base snapshot card.
touch_interaction.visual: Delta layers stack thin and translucent; at the compaction threshold they fold down into a fresh solid base card.

examples.mini_scenario: Each loop turn appends a small delta; after the chain threshold the manager compacts them into a new base so loads stay fast.
examples.pitfall: Never compacting deltas makes load replay an unbounded chain — resume gets slower and more fragile every turn.

examples.title: Load a checkpoint and replay its deltas
examples.intent: Rebuild the exact loop state a resumed task needs.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CheckpointManager::load reads the base TaskCheckpoint and applies each CheckpointDelta via apply_delta in version order, so continue_execution restarts the loop at the right step, iteration, and message history.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking a saved checkpoint pin onto the canvas rehydrates the loop from it in place.
touch_interaction.visual: The base card and its delta layers merge into one restored state card; the loop ring lights back up at the saved step.

examples.mini_scenario: On resume, load replays twelve deltas onto the base; the loop comes back at step 4 with full message context.
examples.pitfall: Applying deltas out of version order reconstructs a corrupt or stale loop state — always replay sequentially.

examples.title: Recover from a corrupted checkpoint
examples.intent: Keep the loop resumable even when a checkpoint file is damaged by a torn write.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CheckpointManager::recover_from_corruption tries the .json.bak backup and otherwise creates a fresh checkpoint, so a crash-truncated file does not permanently strand the task.

outputs_to: restored TaskCheckpoint from backup, or a fresh one

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping a cracked checkpoint pin opens the recovery sheet: restore-from-backup or start-fresh.
touch_interaction.visual: A damaged pin shows a red crack badge; recovery heals it green, or spawns a new blank pin with a warning stripe.

examples.mini_scenario: A checkpoint is truncated by a power loss; recovery loads the .json.bak and the loop resumes from the last good state.
examples.pitfall: Silently starting fresh without surfacing the loss can drop hours of loop progress unnoticed — always show the crack.

examples.title: Encrypt session data at rest
examples.intent: Protect persisted conversations and checkpoints from disk snooping.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EncryptionManager::encrypt wraps bytes with AES-256-GCM and a fresh random nonce; ChatStore and checkpoint writes persist ciphertext, so the loop's entire persistent substrate is confidential without changing loop control.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the persistence node toggles a shield overlay showing which stored cards are encrypted.
touch_interaction.visual: Encrypted cards render with a closed lock glyph; any unencrypted card shows an open-lock amber warning.

examples.mini_scenario: A SavedChat is AES-256-GCM encrypted before hitting disk and decrypted in-process only when the chat is loaded.
examples.pitfall: Reusing a nonce across encryptions under the same key breaks GCM's security guarantee — always generate a fresh nonce.

examples.title: Derive the encryption key from the OS keychain
examples.intent: Bootstrap encryption without a hard-coded key.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EncryptionManager::load_from_keychain reads the passphrase from the OS keychain and derive_key runs PBKDF2 with a per-install salt, so the loop's crypto substrate self-initializes securely at session start.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the persistence node reveals the key source edge feeding the encryption shield.
touch_interaction.visual: A key-ring badge lights green when the keychain supplies the passphrase; a fallback key shows an ephemeral amber badge.

examples.mini_scenario: On startup the manager pulls the passphrase from the keychain, runs derive_key, and decrypts the saved chat list.
examples.pitfall: Falling back to an ephemeral key without warning means data written this session cannot be decrypted later.

examples.title: Persist the conversation to the ChatStore
examples.intent: Save the loop's message history so a named session can be resumed later.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ChatStore::save writes a SavedChat (name, saved_at, model, messages) atomically and encrypted, so resume_named_session can restore the loop's full conversation context.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the message-history strip saves it as a named session card on the store shelf.
touch_interaction.visual: A named session card slots onto the shelf with a lock glyph and timestamp; it pulses once on atomic write.

examples.mini_scenario: The user names and saves the chat; days later resume_named_session decrypts and reloads every message.
examples.pitfall: A non-atomic write interrupted mid-save can leave a truncated, undecryptable chat file — write-then-rename.

examples.title: List sessions while skipping tampered files
examples.intent: Show resumable sessions without crashing on a corrupted or tampered file.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: ChatStore::list returns ChatSummary rows and silently skips files that fail decryption or their GCM auth tag, so the loop presents only valid resume points.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the store shelf fans out the saved session cards; tampered files simply never appear.
touch_interaction.visual: Valid cards render clean with name and saved_at; the shelf shows a small shield badge confirming fail-closed filtering.

examples.mini_scenario: One chat file fails its auth tag; list skips it and the picker shows the remaining valid sessions without an error.
examples.pitfall: Listing a file that fails decryption as if it were valid defers the error to load time and breaks the resume flow.

examples.title: Cache responses for local-first offline use
examples.intent: Serve prior responses and track bandwidth saved when the endpoint is unreachable.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: LocalFirstCoordinator::cache_response stores responses in the LocalCache with size tracking, and stats reports bandwidth_saved_bytes, so the loop can prefer cached data offline and quantify the savings.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the persistence node surfaces a bandwidth-saved gauge fed by the local-first cache.
touch_interaction.visual: The savings gauge grows as cached responses are reused; the node rims blue when OfflineStatus is offline.

examples.mini_scenario: Offline, a repeated request is served from LocalCache and /stats shows the bytes that were not refetched.
examples.pitfall: Unbounded FIFO growth of the local cache eventually evicts the very entries the loop reuses most.

examples.title: Report cache hit rate in /stats
examples.intent: Make the cache's contribution to loop efficiency measurable.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: CacheStats (entry_count, total_size_bytes, hit_rate) surfaces via ToolCache::stats in /stats, letting the loop and operator see whether caching is actually saving act turns and budget.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the cache node opens its stats card with hit rate, entry count, and size.
touch_interaction.visual: A dial shows hit_rate — green when high, amber when the cache is barely helping — with size in a side chip.

examples.mini_scenario: The /stats view shows a 60% tool-cache hit rate, confirming the cache is trimming redundant act steps.
examples.pitfall: Reporting entry_count as a health metric without hit_rate hides a cache that stores much but hits little.

examples.title: Anchor the timeline on a git commit
examples.intent: Align the loop's undo timeline with the repository's own history.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: An EditCheckpoint built with_git_hash records the commit hash and capture_git_state tracks dirty/staged/modified files, giving the timeline a hard VCS boundary the loop must respect when undoing.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the timeline after a commit drops a git-anchor pin marking a hard boundary.
touch_interaction.visual: The git pin renders with a short commit-hash badge and a heavier boundary line that undo markers cannot cross silently.

examples.mini_scenario: After the agent commits, the timeline gets a git-anchored checkpoint so a later /undo knows where the committed baseline sits.
examples.pitfall: Treating a git-anchored checkpoint like an ordinary undo point can rewind past a commit and desync the working tree.

examples.title: Zeroize the encryption key on drop
examples.intent: Ensure the session key never lingers in memory after use.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: EncryptionManager's Drop impl calls zeroize on the key bytes when the manager is dropped at session teardown, so the loop's crypto substrate leaves no key residue for a memory scrape.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the persistence node off the canvas at session end visibly scrubs its key glyph.
touch_interaction.visual: The key badge dissolves into zeros as the node tears down; the shield overlay fades with it.

examples.mini_scenario: At session end the manager drops and its 32-byte key is zeroized before the allocation is freed.
examples.pitfall: Copying the key into another struct without matching zeroization leaves a plaintext key copy behind in memory.
